figures.caption: FIG. 13. (a) The Mohr circle is a graphical tool that is used to determine transformations of a rank 2 tensor (such as stress) under rotation. The stress components for a given coordinate system are represented by points A and B, which form a diameter of the circle. The transformed stress components upon a rotation of the coordinate system by angle ψ can be found by a rotation of these points by 2ψ around the circle. The point C, which has a tangent that passes through the origin, corresponds to the orientation of a shear plane (at an angle φ to the x axis) with the largest ratio of shear to normal stress. (b) The stress angle 2φ [COA in (a)] as a function of height for θ=20° (○), 22° (□), 24° (◇), and 26° (△). The results are for Model H3 with H=40.
